title: REST APIs on network equipment: authentication, verbs and pagination

videos.script: In lesson 1, the script talked to the router the way a person does. It typed commands and read the screen. {{cli}} That works, and it is fragile. A new software version changes one column, and the script reads the wrong number. {{fragile}} Most equipment now has a second door, an API. The script sends a request to an address, and the router answers in JSON: named fields, no screen to parse. {{api}} In this lesson you log in and get a token. You read interfaces and routes. You create a static route, change it, and delete it, and watch each verb answer with its own status code. {{verbs}} Then the parts that break scripts in production. Lists that come one page at a time. A router that says too fast, and tells you how long to wait. And a certificate that proves the router is the router. {{hard}} By the end, the script is a small client you can reuse against any router in the lab. {{client}}
